methodology: Use AutoModel hidden-state extraction as the inference entry point, represent each sentence independently with raw last-layer DistilBERT pooled embeddings rather than sentence-transformers sentence embeddings, and score with cosine-similarity thresholding, differing from the MiniLM bi-encoder variant by relying on untuned base-model features and from classifier variants by using no task head at all.
plan: 1) In one code cell install transformers, datasets, scikit-learn, and tqdm; 2) import torch, numpy, load_dataset, AutoTokenizer, AutoModel, accuracy_score, f1_score, classification_report, and tqdm; 3) set device to torch.device('mps' if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else 'cpu') and print it; 4) choose model_name = 'distilbert-base-uncased', load tokenizer and AutoModel, move the model to device, and set eval mode; 5) load glue/mrpc validation and extract sentence1, sentence2, and y_true; 6) write a small mean_pool function that averages token embeddings using the attention mask, then L2-normalizes the pooled vectors; 7) run batched encoding separately for sentence1 and sentence2 with truncation and padding, obtain last_hidden_state, mean-pool with the mask, normalize, and store sentence embeddings on CPU; 8) compute cosine similarities for aligned pairs and threshold them once with a fixed value such as 0.85 to get y_pred; 9) compute accuracy, F1, and classification_report; 10) print several examples with cosine scores and the first 10 errors; 11) create a summary dict with dataset, split, model, device, threshold, num_examples, accuracy, and f1.
